propositions.text: Mr. Paul Uchemadu Adiele and his minor children seek judicial review of an officer's refusal of his open work permit application
The open work permit was to accompany his wife, a student at the University of Saskatchewan

paragraphs.summary: The applicants seek judicial review of an officer's refusal of an open work permit to accompany the applicant's wife, a student.

propositions.text: The Principal Applicant's application was refused on February 2, 2024 due to insufficient evidence of wife's full-time student status at a DLI

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker refused the application on February 2, 2024 for insufficient evidence of wife's full-time student status.

propositions.text: On February 5, 2024, the Principal Applicant requested reconsideration of the refusal decision
On February 7, 2024, IRCC acknowledged receipt of reconsideration request and stated no response in 10 working days means refusal of reconsideration
IRCC advised reapplication is possible and will be decided on its own merits

paragraphs.summary: The applicant requested reconsideration; IRCC acknowledged it and stated no response in 10 days means refusal, advising reapplication is possible.

propositions.text: In May 2025 affidavit, the Principal Applicant deposed he did not hear further from IRCC within 10 days about reconsideration
He filed application for leave and judicial review about the February 2, 2024 decision on February 29, 2024

paragraphs.summary: The applicant deposed no response from IRCC on reconsideration and filed judicial review application on February 29, 2024.

propositions.text: On October 21, 2024, IRCC determined sufficient evidence of spouse's full-time student status but refused open work permit based on funds

paragraphs.summary: IRCC later found sufficient evidence of spouse's status but refused the work permit due to insufficient funds.

propositions.text: Following a Production Order, IRCC filed the Certified Tribunal Record (CTR)
The Minister objected to inclusion in CTR of materials about reconsideration request

paragraphs.summary: IRCC filed the Certified Tribunal Record; the Minister objected to including reconsideration materials.

propositions.text: An amended CTR was filed excluding materials about the reconsideration request

paragraphs.summary: An amended Certified Tribunal Record was filed excluding reconsideration materials.

propositions.text: The Order granting leave was issued on April 16, 2025

paragraphs.summary: The court granted leave on April 16, 2025.

propositions.text: The Principal Applicant argues the Officer's decision on wife's full-time student status is unreasonable and should be set aside
He submits the Officer breached procedural fairness by denying opportunity to address sufficient funds issue in October 21, 2024 decision

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the decision on wife's status is unreasonable and alleges procedural fairness breach regarding funds issue.

propositions.text: The Respondent submits the judicial review application is moot since the open work permit was reconsidered and refused on October 21, 2024
No judicial review was filed regarding the October 21, 2024 decision

paragraphs.summary: The respondent argues the application is moot because the permit was reconsidered and refused later, with no review filed on that decision.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness issues are reviewable on the standard of correctness, per Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Khosa

paragraphs.summary: Procedural fairness issues are reviewed on correctness standard, per Khosa.

propositions.text: Following Vavilov, merits of decision are reviewable on reasonableness standard

paragraphs.summary: Merits of decision are reviewed on reasonableness standard following Vavilov.

propositions.text: Reasonableness requires decision to show justification, transparency, intelligibility, and be justified by relevant facts and law, per Vavilov para 99

paragraphs.summary: Reasonableness requires justification, transparency, intelligibility, and justification by facts and law per Vavilov.

propositions.text: The February 2, 2024 decision is subject of judicial review
The Principal Applicant seeks orders quashing refusal and inadmissibility decisions, directing grant or re-determination by different officer, or further orders

paragraphs.summary: The applicant seeks to quash the refusal and inadmissibility decisions and requests grant or re-determination by another officer.

propositions.text: Prime Minister v. Hameed sets out two-step analysis for mootness: live controversy and discretion to hear moot case
Second step considers adversarial context, judicial economy, and court's role

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court of Appeal in Hameed sets a two-step mootness test considering live controversy and discretion factors.

propositions.text: Application of mootness principle is discretionary for the Court

paragraphs.summary: The court states mootness application is discretionary.

propositions.text: Respondent did not raise mootness at leave stage but did so in Further Memorandum

paragraphs.summary: The respondent raised mootness only in the Further Memorandum, not at leave stage.

propositions.text: Revised CTR excludes reconsideration decision but it is attached as exhibit to applicant's Further affidavit
Respondent did not object to inclusion of reconsideration decision exhibit

paragraphs.summary: The reconsideration decision is excluded from CTR but attached to applicant's affidavit; respondent did not object.

propositions.text: The reconsideration decision does not identify the decision-maker
Respondent bases mootness argument on the reconsideration decision

paragraphs.summary: The reconsideration decision lacks decision-maker identity; respondent relies on it for mootness argument.

propositions.text: The court declines to dismiss the application on grounds of mootness

paragraphs.summary: The court exercises discretion and declines to dismiss the application as moot.

propositions.text: A live controversy remains between the parties regarding the application for an open work permit
It is unnecessary to address other elements of the mootness discussion

paragraphs.summary: The court finds a live controversy remains about the open work permit application and declines to address mootness further.

propositions.text: The Applicants submitted the February 2, 2024 decision was made without regard to the evidence
The decision fails to meet the standard of reasonableness

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the Applicants that the February 2, 2024 decision ignored evidence and is unreasonable.

propositions.text: It is unnecessary to address procedural fairness
The procedural fairness argument is not appropriately raised in this judicial review application

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it unnecessary to address procedural fairness, noting the argument is inappropriately raised here.

propositions.text: The application for judicial review is granted
The decision is set aside
The matter is remitted to a different officer for re-determination
There is no question for certification

paragraphs.summary: The court grants judicial review, sets aside the decision, remits the matter for re-determination, and finds no question for certification.
